# pantechdynamics_cloud_connection (Resource)

A read-only connection Pantech Migrate uses to scan an account in another cloud and plan its move to Pantech. Nothing is shared when it is created: its setup says what to run in the other cloud. AWS, Google Cloud, Azure and Huawei Cloud are federated: run the setup there, then send what it printed with pantechdynamics_cloud_connection_federation. DigitalOcean, Hetzner, Linode, Vultr, Contabo and OpenStack are read by the Pantech Migrate agent, which you run with a read-only token that never leaves your machine; enroll it with `pantech migrate agent enroll`. Scans, plans and moves are one-shot jobs and are not managed by Terraform. Destroying the connection removes it and its scans; migration plans made from it stay. Owners and admins only; at most 10 connections.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A connection to an AWS account. Its setup_template is a CloudFormation
# template for a read-only role only Pantech can assume; create the stack
# (here with the AWS provider), then send its RoleArn output with
# pantechdynamics_cloud_connection_federation.
resource "pantechdynamics_cloud_connection" "aws" {
  name = "Production AWS"
}

resource "aws_cloudformation_stack" "pantech_migrate" {
  name          = "pantech-migrate"
  template_body = pantechdynamics_cloud_connection.aws.setup_template
  capabilities  = ["CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM"]
}

# A Google Cloud connection: run setup_template (a gcloud script), then send
# what it printed with pantechdynamics_cloud_connection_federation.
resource "pantechdynamics_cloud_connection" "gcp" {
  cloud = "gcp"
  name  = "Production GCP"
}

# A Hetzner connection, read by the Pantech Migrate agent you run with a
# read-only token that never leaves your machine. Enroll the agent with
# `pantech migrate agent enroll <id>`.
resource "pantechdynamics_cloud_connection" "hetzner" {
  cloud = "hetzner"
  name  = "Hetzner"
}

output "hetzner_token_how_to" {
  value = pantechdynamics_cloud_connection.hetzner.agent_token_how_to
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) A name such as "Production AWS", 1 to 100 characters. Changes in place.

### Optional

- `cloud` (String) The cloud (the API's provider field; provider is a name Terraform reserves): "aws" (the default), "gcp", "azure", "huawei", "digitalocean", "hetzner", "linode", "vultr", "contabo" or "openstack". The pantechdynamics_cloud_providers data source says which this platform offers. Changing it replaces the connection.

### Read-Only

- `access` (String) "federated" or "agent": how Pantech reads this cloud.
- `agent_container_command` (String) Agent providers: how to run the agent as a container.
- `agent_enroll_command` (String) Agent providers: the enrollment command, with <ENROLLMENT_CODE> where the one-time code goes.
- `agent_image` (String) Agent providers: the Pantech Migrate agent's container image.
- `agent_run_command` (String) Agent providers: how to run the agent.
- `agent_token_how_to` (String) Agent providers: how to make the read-only token.
- `agent_token_variables` (List of String) Agent providers: the environment variables the agent reads the read-only token from, on your machine.
- `audience` (String) The audience every token carries; null for agent providers.
- `created_at` (String) When the connection was created, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.
- `external_account_id` (String) The source account: an AWS account, a Google Cloud pool's project number, an Azure tenant, or what the agent reported. Null until connected.
- `failure_code` (String) Why the last check failed, such as "permission_missing"; null when it did not.
- `failure_message` (String) What to do about the failure; null when there is none.
- `id` (String) Identifier of the connection, starting with ccn_.
- `issuer_url` (String) Pantech's identity provider URL, which the other cloud trusts; null for agent providers.
- `permissions` (List of String) Every read-only permission the setup grants.
- `quick_create_url` (String) AWS only: opens AWS's create-stack page with the template and this connection filled in; null when not offered.
- `setup_files` (Map of String) Further setup files by name, such as a Terraform version of the setup or JSON documents to paste.
- `setup_template` (String) The main setup file: AWS's CloudFormation template (JSON), Google Cloud's gcloud script, Azure's Azure CLI script, Huawei Cloud's steps, or, for agent providers, how to make a read-only token.
- `setup_template_format` (String) The setup_template's format: "cloudformation", "shell", "markdown" or "agent".
- `status` (String) "awaiting_role" (federated: waiting for what the setup printed), "awaiting_agent" (waiting for the Pantech Migrate agent), "verifying", "connected" or "failed".
- `subject` (String) The subject the other cloud's trust policy requires: this connection's id.
- `verified_at` (String) When the connection was last verified, in RFC 3339 UTC, to the second.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A connection is imported by its id.
terraform import pantechdynamics_cloud_connection.aws ccn_06gk3x9tq7m2v8r4y1c5d0zp8w
```
